news.headline: First Phosphate secures Swiss export support for up to US$212.5M in project financing
news.summary: First Phosphate Corp. CEO John Passalacqua joined Steve Darling from Proactive to discuss a significant financing milestone for the company's integrated phosphate development strategy, announcing that First Phosphate has received a Letter of Support from Swiss Export Risk Insurance (SERV) for approximately US$212.5 million in potential financing support for its Quebec-based phosphate project. The support is intended to facilitate the purchase of Swiss machinery and equipment for First Phosphate's planned igneous phosphate mining operation, as well as goods and services required for the construction of its proposed processing facility in the Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean region of Quebec. Passalacqua described the development as a major endorsement of the project's strategic importance and its growing international partnerships as the company works to establish a North American supply chain for lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery materials. Under the framework outlined in the Letter of Support, SERV is prepared to consider insurance and guarantee coverage for buyer-credit financing based on an assumed eligible Swiss export contract value of approximately US$250 million. Based on that amount, SERV could support financing of approximately US$212.5 million, representing 85% of the eligible contract value. Should the final value of Swiss-sourced equipment and services exceed the current estimate, SERV indicated it would be prepared to consider a proportionally larger financing package. According to the company, SERV's support could substantially enhance the project's access to competitive financing by providing export credit guarantees that reduce risk for lenders. In line with current OECD export credit guidelines, SERV may provide coverage for up to 95% of the eligible financed amount. The financing package could include not only the majority of the export contract value but also eligible local project costs of up to 50% of the export contract value, capitalized interest incurred during construction and applicable export credit agency premiums. First Phosphate noted that a sufficient portion of the project is expected to be sourced from Switzerland, making it eligible for SERV support. In addition, SERV may explore reinsurance arrangements with other export credit agencies to provide coverage for significant project components sourced from outside Switzerland. Passalacqua said the support reflects growing international confidence in First Phosphate's strategy of developing a fully integrated phosphate supply chain focused on supplying the rapidly expanding lithium iron phosphate battery market.
